For a company that made its name manufacturing intelligent electric vehicles, the prospect of producing a humanoid robot every two and a half minutes represents a remarkable evolution of its industrial ambitions. And that is precisely what Chinese technology company XPeng is working towards.
At its AI Day 2026 event in Guangzhou, XPeng unveiled the latest generation of its general-purpose humanoid robot, Iron, outlining a strategy that brings together artificial intelligence, automotive manufacturing expertise and a new commercial ecosystem for robotics.
Mass production is scheduled to begin in January 2027, marking an important transition from technology development to commercial operations.
He Xiaopeng, chairman and CEO of XPeng, says: “Humanoid robotics is reaching the point where the industry must move beyond demonstrations and prove that robots can create value in the real world.
“That requires more than capable hardware or intelligent models. It requires reliable products, high-quality data, scalable manufacturing and continuous learning through deployment. XPeng Iron brings these capabilities together as we prepare for commercial deployment and mass production is scheduled to begin in January 2027.”
Central to XPeng’s approach is the simultaneous development of the robot’s intelligence and physical capabilities.
Its Turing physical AI architecture incorporates three interconnected systems responsible for higher-level reasoning and task planning, real-time decision-making and the direct control of physical movements.
The latest generation of Iron features 76 degrees of freedom, including a dexterous hand with 21 degrees of freedom, more than 1,500 tactile sensing points, 3D vision and 360-degree environmental perception.
Three proprietary Turing AI chips provide a combined 2,250 trillion operations per second of effective computing power.
The robot is designed to recognize people, retain conversational context, navigate autonomously, monitor its operational health and recharge itself before returning to work.
XPeng has also incorporated five layers of safety protection, including collision detection, torque limits and emergency-stop mechanisms.

items.excerpt:
Robbyant , an embodied AI company within Ant Group, has announced the open-source release of two AI models designed to improve robots’ ability to map physical environments, retain spatial information and navigate autonomously.
The models – LingBot-Map 2.0 and LingBot-Navi – address two significant challenges in autonomous robotics: the accumulation of mapping errors over long distances and the inability of some navigation systems to retain knowledge of their surroundings between tasks.
These challenges affect a range of physical AI applications, from warehouse logistics and industrial automation to last-mile delivery and domestic robotics.
LingBot-Map 2.0 builds on the original model released in April 2026, introducing an internal error correction mechanism inspired by memory reconsolidation in the human brain.
Called Geometric Context Reshaping (GCR), the mechanism enables the model to reuse previously extracted geometric information and correct its internal spatial memory without having to process images again.
Unlike conventional external correction methods, which adjust a robot’s recorded trajectory, GCR updates the model’s internal representation of its surroundings, providing a more reliable reference for subsequent movement.
The system also incorporates LingBot-Vision, Robbyant’s visual foundation model, to improve geometric accuracy.
According to Robbyant, testing over a 5.2 km urban trajectory involving nearly 19,000 frames showed that average trajectory error fell from 31.12 meters in the original model to 4.72 meters in version 2.0 – a reduction of nearly 85 percent.
The company also reports that the model ranked first across three dense 3D reconstruction benchmarks: CroCoDL, EuRoC and Oxford.
Built on LingBot-Map 2.0, LingBot-Navi introduces persistent spatial memory, enabling robots to retain information about objects and locations between missions.
Rather than repeatedly exploring familiar environments, robots can retrieve previously acquired spatial information in response to natural language commands and use it to plan more efficient routes.
The model also supports on-device operation, allowing user commands and environmental data to remain local, reducing latency and supporting data privacy.
In simulation tests using a subset of the GOAT-Bench public benchmark, LingBot-Navi achieved a task success rate of 68.60 percent, outperforming the best of six comparative methods by 10.36 percentage points.

items.excerpt:
Moving an ordinary household is one thing. Moving a home library, hundreds of vinyl records, artwork, vintage cameras, or years of hobby equipment is a different kind of job. These aren’t just boxes of belongings. They’re collections you’ve spent time, money, and plenty of patience putting together. Some pieces may be rare, fragile, or impossible to replace.
The challenge is getting everything to the new address without damage, missing parts, or losing track of how it was organized. Finding the right crew can help coordinate transportation, but protecting a collection starts well before moving day. Here’s how to make the process manageable.
Collections need more planning than ordinary household goods because their items often vary in size, shape, material, and value. A vinyl collection, for example, might include records, sleeves, inserts, and special editions that all need to stay together. A library may be arranged by author, subject, or a personal system that makes perfect sense to its owner and nobody else.
Packing everything randomly into spare boxes can destroy that organization. It can also make unpacking a frustrating guessing game. Treat the collection as a separate moving project. Give it its own inventory, packing materials, labels, and designated space in the new home. For a longer haul, experienced movers from Los Angeles to Sacramento can plan the collection as its own part of the shipment rather than mixing it in with everything else.
Before wrapping anything, make a record of what you own. A simple spreadsheet is usually enough. Include each item’s name, description, condition, approximate value, and the box number where it will be packed. Take photographs of valuable, rare, fragile, or sentimental pieces. For artwork, photograph the front, back, frame, and any existing damage. For collectibles, capture serial numbers, signatures, identifying marks, and accessories.
Keep receipts, appraisals, certificates of authenticity, and other relevant paperwork in a separate digital folder. This documentation can help establish an item’s condition and value if something goes wrong during the move. It might feel like extra work, but a few minutes with a camera can save you a serious headache later.

items.description: Most small shops I walk into have a robot arm, a CNC cell, or a sensor array doing real work, and a bookkeeper in the back office still retyping job numbers into a paper invoice at 6 p.m. Two halves of the same business that never speak to each other. That gap costs you more […]
items.excerpt:
Most small shops I walk into have a robot arm, a CNC cell, or a sensor array doing real work, and a bookkeeper in the back office still retyping job numbers into a paper invoice at 6 p.m. Two halves of the same business that never speak to each other.
That gap costs you more than you think. A finished install sits in limbo until someone remembers to bill it, and every idle day is working capital you already spent on parts and labor. Getting paid faster starts with treating billing as part of your operations layer, not as paperwork that trails behind it. If you run a field crew or a service bench, part of the fix is simply picking better invoicing software that can fire a bill from a phone the moment the job closes.
Here’s the promise: by the end of this piece you’ll know how to wire your completed work directly to your cash flow, which signals matter, and where the whole thing breaks if you let it. Call it the close-the-loop model. Work finishes, a bill goes out, money comes in, and nobody has to be the human reminder in the middle.
The leak has a shape. It’s not one dramatic failure. It’s a hundred small delays. A technician finishes a repair at 3 p.m. and means to write it up later. A project manager marks a job complete but the billing trigger lives in a spreadsheet someone updates on Fridays. A customer disputes a line item because your handwritten note didn’t match what they were quoted.
Add those up and you’re floating your own customers a loan you never agreed to. That’s a real cost on a balance sheet, and it’s boring enough that most owners ignore it because the money does eventually arrive.
Compare that with a shop that closes the loop. Equipment signals completion, a pre-approved rate card generates the invoice, the customer gets it by text before they leave the site, and payment lands in days instead of weeks. Same work, wildly different cash position.
Trying to automate everything at once is how you blow a quarter’s budget on integrations nobody uses. Instead, sort your billing triggers into three buckets and do them in order.
My opinion: most operators should live in tier one for at least a full quarter before they touch tier two. You’ll learn the edge cases on small money and avoid an ugly surprise on a six-figure contract.

A robotic packing line can continue operating even if a separate digital display showing its output stops updating. The machinery remains productive, but supervisors may lose access to the information they use to coordinate packing, pallet collection and dispatch.
That makes the computer behind the display more than an accessory. Where signage helps keep people informed on the factory floor , the computer’s operating conditions and failure behaviour deserve attention during system design.
The computer’s location is often dictated by the display it serves, available cabling and maintenance access. Beside a robotic production line or inside a loading-bay enclosure, the task is to choose hardware that can operate reliably in that position.
Where possible, temperatures should be measured at the computer’s intended location under representative operating conditions. A factory floor could reach 28°C, while heat accumulating inside the enclosure takes the player’s surroundings to 46°C. In this illustrative case, a computer with a maximum operating temperature of 40°C would be unsuitable, even though the surrounding factory environment remains within that limit.
Cold conditions matter too. Equipment in an unheated loading bay may need to start before the morning shift, when temperatures are lower than during normal working hours.
For these installations, wide-temperature digital signage computers can provide operating ranges suited to the measured extremes. Selection should account for both startup and continuous operation, with enough allowance for seasonal changes and heat generated during production.
Choosing a computer with a broader temperature range does not compensate for an unsuitable enclosure or configuration.
Operating temperature ratings can depend on the computer’s hardware configuration and cooling requirements. For example, a system fitted with an industrial wide-temperature solid-state drive may support a broader operating temperature range than the same system configured with a conventional hard disk drive.
Manufacturers may also specify minimum airflow requirements or other installation conditions for extended-temperature operation. Installing a computer in a sealed cabinet without accounting for heat removal could therefore compromise its reliability, even if its published temperature rating appears suitable.

A windshield does more than protect you from wind, rain, and road debris. In many modern cars, it also helps safety systems monitor the road.
These cars have cameras mounted behind the windshield that help detect vehicles, pedestrians, and road markings. The cameras need a clear view of the road to work properly. Even the shape of the glass and the camera’s position can affect how these systems work.
ADAS stands for advanced driver assistance systems. These systems use cameras, sensors, and software to help drivers stay safe on the road.

A windshield must do more than fit the vehicle. Its clarity, shape, and camera mounting position can all affect the information a camera collects.

This can make it harder for the system to process the information correctly.

items.title: Black Friday 2026: The Logistics Bill Arrives After Checkout
items.description: Black Friday sales are only part of the story. Parcel surcharges, fulfillment decisions and returns determine how much holiday revenue retailers keep. The post Black Friday 2026: The Logistics Bill Arrives After Checkout appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Black Friday has traditionally been measured by what consumers spend. Retailers report sales growth, analysts track transaction volumes, and the financial press compares this year’s numbers with last year’s records. But for logistics and supply chain executives, the more important question comes after the transaction: How much of that revenue will remain once the order has been fulfilled, delivered, and potentially returned?
The distinction matters particularly in 2026. According to Adobe's holiday shopping forecast , U.S. consumers are expected to spend $12.9 billion online on Black Friday, an increase of 9.2% from last year. Cyber Monday is projected to reach $15.1 billion, while online spending for the full November–December holiday season is expected to total $275.1 billion, up 6.7%. Meanwhile, the National Retail Federation forecasts $1.013 trillion in total holiday retail sales, representing 4.2% growth. The two forecasts cover different retail measures, but both point toward another substantial holiday selling season.
That should be encouraging news for retailers. It is also a reminder that transaction growth and profitable fulfillment are not necessarily the same thing. Every additional order creates obligations across warehousing, transportation, labor, customer service, and reverse logistics. When promotional discounts are already reducing product margins, the economics of fulfilling those obligations deserve considerably more attention.
Black Friday is no longer the beginning of the holiday shopping season. Promotional activity now extends through October, November, and December, with retailers using successive events to stimulate demand. Adobe expects U.S. online spending in October alone to reach $95.8 billion, an 8% year-over-year increase.
For logistics organizations, this changes the nature of peak season planning. Rather than preparing for a concentrated surge following Thanksgiving, distribution networks must manage successive demand waves while maintaining normal replenishment, store support, and e-commerce operations. The challenge is not simply processing a higher volume of orders. It is managing the variability in order composition, delivery destinations, labor requirements, and transportation capacity.

A truck crash on the Van Wyck or the BQE leaves two kinds of evidence behind. One is visible: the damage, the scene, the witnesses.
The other sits inside the truck, in an electronic logging device (ELD), an engine control module and often a camera, and some of it can be overwritten within days.
That second kind is why choosing a Queens truck accident lawyer is partly a technical decision.
This guide compares nine firms with Queens offices, using what each one publicly says about its fees, languages and handling of onboard truck data.
ELDs log hours, not driving behavior. Under 49 CFR 395.26, an ELD automatically records date, time, location, engine hours, vehicle miles and driver, vehicle and carrier identifiers. That is the core reason why truck drivers need ELDs .
FMCSA guidance from March 2022 confirms ELDs are not required to collect speed, braking or steering data, and while a truck is moving they create roughly hourly intermediate records.
Engine and vehicle control units fill the gap, sometimes. In its investigation of the February 2025 Interstate 80 tunnel crash near Green River, Wyoming, the NTSB recovered vehicle speed, engine speed and steering, brake and accelerator inputs from truck control modules.
It also found one truck’s VECU running 10 minutes and 1 second slow and another more than two hours slow, so clocks must be reconciled before any timeline is trusted.
Video settles disputes. In the NTSB’s final report on a July 2025 multivehicle crash in Charlotte, dashcam footage showed a truck had been parked on the shoulder for 1 minute and 28 seconds when it was struck.
Retention is short. Carriers must keep duty-status records for six months under 49 CFR 395.8(k)(1).
Nothing comparable protects engine events or footage, and guidance from the Scientific Working Group on Digital Evidence warns that power cycles during vehicle handling can cause data loss.

A crash on I-490 at rush hour or a slide through a snowy intersection on East Avenue can leave you with medical bills, a damaged car and an insurance adjuster asking for a recorded statement within days. The lawyer you call first shapes almost everything that follows.
The choice matters more now than it did two years ago. New York changed its motor vehicle fault rules in 2026, so a Rochester driver who is found mostly at fault can now walk away with nothing. This guide compares seven Rochester car accident firms on the details that actually separate them, then explains what to ask before you sign.
For decades, New York let an injured driver recover something even when they were mostly to blame. That changed for motor vehicle cases. Under CPLR 1411(b), added on May 26, 2026, a claimant whose fault exceeds that of the defendants being sued recovers nothing. An exact 50/50 split does not trigger the bar.
The same law removed the 90/180-day category from New York’s serious injury threshold. That category let people with temporary injuries that kept them from normal activities for 90 of the first 180 days sue for pain and suffering. Those claims now have to fit one of the remaining categories, such as a fracture, significant disfigurement or a permanent limitation.
Both changes apply to lawsuits started on or after May 26, 2026, regardless of when the crash happened. In practice, fault evidence and medical documentation now carry more weight than ever, so a firm’s investigation habits matter as much as its marketing.

Europe’s industrial strength has traditionally been built on generations of accumulated knowledge – the expertise of people who understand how to work with materials, operate machinery, manufacture products and manage complex production processes. But what if that knowledge could be transferred to robots and become a commercially valuable asset in its own right?
That is one of the ideas behind a new initiative in the Spanish region of Aragón, where German robotics company Neura Robotics , the regional government and agri-food company Costa Group are joining forces to develop an industrial ecosystem around physical AI.
The three partners have signed a memorandum of understanding to establish Neura Gym Aragón and develop a surrounding Physical AI Model Zone, with an opening targeted for mid-2027.
The project envisages investment in the tens of millions of euros, with Neura Robotics taking a leading investment role.
Rather than simply encouraging businesses to introduce more robots into their operations, the initiative aims to give companies the infrastructure to develop robotic capabilities based on their own industrial expertise – and potentially generate new sources of revenue from that knowledge.
David Reger, founder and CEO of Neura Robotics, says: “The knowledge of how to produce, handle and assemble things is one of Europe’s greatest assets. With our partners in Aragón, we want to give companies the tools to turn that knowledge into robotic capabilities they can use, improve and build a business around.
“A company that develops a valuable skill should benefit when others use it. Our ambition is to connect Europe’s industrial strengths while keeping control and economic opportunity with the people and businesses that create them. That is how expertise developed here can become technology that customers around the world need.”
One of the challenges facing the emerging physical AI industry is that intelligence developed in the digital world does not necessarily translate into an ability to perform useful tasks in the physical world.
Robots need to understand how to interact with objects, materials, tools and environments that can vary considerably from one workplace to another.
And much of the knowledge required to perform these tasks resides not in computer systems or instruction manuals, but in the experience of people working in factories, warehouses, farms and other industrial environments.

items.title: ETH Zurich develops tiny sensor that enables silent communication with AI
items.description: Researchers at ETH Zurich in Switzerland have developed a miniature wearable sensor that enables users to communicate with artificial intelligence without speaking aloud or moving their lips. Called InvisiSpeech, the device fits between a back molar and the cheek, detecting the subtle vibrations generated when users silently form words with their tongues. These signals are […]
items.excerpt:
Researchers at ETH Zurich in Switzerland have developed a miniature wearable sensor that enables users to communicate with artificial intelligence without speaking aloud or moving their lips.
Called InvisiSpeech, the device fits between a back molar and the cheek, detecting the subtle vibrations generated when users silently form words with their tongues.
These signals are transmitted wirelessly to a smartphone, where an AI model decodes them into commands.
The technology has been developed by researchers at ETH Zurich’s Sensing, Interaction & Perception Lab (SIPLAB), led by Christian Holz, professor of computer science.
The device resembles a small dental brace and contains a sensor, a battery and electronics for wireless data transmission. It remains completely hidden from outside view when worn.
Unlike brain-computer interfaces, InvisiSpeech does not measure brain signals or require implants or surgical intervention.
Yijing Jiang, a doctoral student working on the project, says: “The device itself is so small that it can be worn comfortably in your mouth.”
In studies involving 15 participants, InvisiSpeech correctly recognized around 90 percent of 50 predefined English commands, requiring only brief calibration for each individual.
The researchers found that background noise had little effect on recognition accuracy, offering a potential advantage over conventional microphone-based interfaces in noisy environments.
Applications already tested include switching electronic devices on and off, retrieving information during meetings and translating foreign-language content using AI glasses.
Holz says: “InvisiSpeech enables us to interact in fundamentally new ways: the invisible input of commands to an AI via natural language.”
The technology could also provide new opportunities for accessible communication and discreet interaction with wearable computing devices.
The researchers ultimately aim to move beyond predefined commands and enable users to conduct natural, private conversations with AI assistants.
Such a system could operate in a similar way to existing AI voice assistants, but with users silently articulating their questions and receiving spoken responses through earphones.
This could allow people to interact with AI while traveling on public transport, attending meetings or accessing personal information without being overheard.
However, further development is required before the technology becomes practical for widespread everyday use.

With five days left, I allowed myself a little fun. When you have a Ferrari, every now and then you want to take it out on the track. So I asked myself: what if I tried to generate videos?
I picked LTX-2.5 from Lightricks, which generates video and sound together. By the end, once the models were loaded, a 10-second clip with sound took 22 to 23 s to generate, on half of the machine. Here is the result.
I had two goals. The first was to see how easy it is to generate videos with diffusers on Trainium3. Not the simple clips from the examples: I wanted to make short films from a script, closer to a real use case, like drafting a movie. The second was performance. Renovating your home while still living in it sounds like a good way to save money. No temporary rental, no moving your furniture twice, no figuring out where the dog is supposed to sleep. Sounds easy enough, right?
Well, anybody who’s lived through a major renovation knows there’s a little more to it. Between construction noise, dust, restricted access, and contractors coming and going, your daily routine can get turned upside down pretty quickly.
Sometimes even exterior projects can create plenty of disruption. A Сape Сod roof replacement service might not require you to leave the house, for example, but you’ll certainly want to prepare for noise, material deliveries, and temporary restrictions around the property. The trick is planning ahead and knowing which inconveniences you can live with.
Before the work starts, take an honest look at the project. Replacing siding or roofing is generally easier to manage while staying indoors than renovating the only bathroom or completely rebuilding the kitchen. Ask your contractor how much of the house will be affected, whether utilities need to be disconnected, and how long the noisiest stages are expected to last. Consider these factors:
If the answers start looking uncomfortable, consider alternative accommodation for at least part of the project.
Not all renovations are created equal. Exterior work, such as roofing, siding, and window replacement, can often be completed without making the interior unlivable. Still, expect hammering, ladders, equipment, and workers moving around the property.
Interior renovations are another story. Kitchen remodeling can leave you without cooking facilities, while bathroom renovations may create serious problems if there’s only one bathroom in the house. Major structural work, electrical upgrades, and extensive plumbing projects can also involve temporary utility interruptions.
Here’s a useful approach: ask your contractor to identify the most disruptive phases before construction begins. You don’t need every minor detail figured out, but you should know when the house will be loud, dusty, or temporarily inaccessible.
Construction dust has a remarkable talent for getting into places you’d never expect. Cover furniture with protective sheets, remove fragile decorations, and move valuables away from active work areas. items.description: Does global forwarding scale produce better service? DSV’s Schenker integration shows why local execution and exception ownership matter to shippers. The post DHL, DSV and Kuehne+Nagel: Does Forwarding Scale Improve Service? appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Global freight forwarding has consolidated around companies with broad networks, purchasing leverage and increasingly sophisticated technology platforms. Yet the shipper does not buy a map of a forwarder’s offices. It buys reliable local handoffs, accurate documentation, responsive exceptions and a commercially coherent service across jurisdictions. DSV’s integration of Schenker provides an especially useful test of whether a larger network actually improves those outcomes.
In its October 21, 2026 third-quarter report , DSV said gross profit increased 2.3% year over year while operating profit before special items rose 19.5%, with integration synergies contributing to results. At the same time, the Road division experienced lower productivity and negative volume growth linked to operational issues in Europe after the Schenker integration; the company said operations normalized toward the end of the quarter. That combination is significant: financial progress at the group level can coexist with local execution disruption that directly affects individual customers.
In the same October 2026 report , DSV identified operational challenges in European Road following the Schenker integration and said activity normalized toward the end of the quarter. The company reported integration synergies while acknowledging that remaining Road-related synergies and some Group benefits would extend into 2027. That is not proof that consolidation fails. It shows why a shipper should separate a corporate integration’s financial trajectory from actual booking, movement and customs performance in its own lanes.
The implication is not that consolidation fails. The more disciplined interpretation is that executives should separate expected synergies from observable shipper outcomes. Back-office rationalization and network purchasing can improve the provider’s economics, but customers evaluate booking accuracy, transit consistency, customs quality and exception resolution. If a global savings initiative creates unresolved branch-level handoffs, the benefits may accrue to the forwarder before they accrue to the customer.
Forwarding customers need global reach but experience the service locally. A consolidation that simplifies contracts and improves systems may help multinational shippers coordinate shipments. items.title: The Future of Retail Is Not Inventory-Free. It Is Inventory by Design.
items.description: Physical retail is not disappearing. The next competitive advantage comes from assigning stores, inventory, and fulfillment assets deliberate roles based on total cost to serve. The post The Future of Retail Is Not Inventory-Free. It Is Inventory by Design. appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Will the retail store eventually become a showroom, with customers examining samples and having everything delivered to their homes?
For some products, absolutely. For all products, no. And that distinction is the basis of a more useful discussion about the future of retail.
A furniture retailer does not need 40 identical sofas sitting behind every showroom. A grocery customer buying milk for dinner has a very different expectation. A shopper evaluating a premium appliance may want to see and compare models, but may be perfectly happy scheduling delivery and installation. A customer buying a common household item may regard a two-day wait as a service failure.
These are not variations on the same problem. They are different combinations of demand, product economics, inventory requirements, and service expectations. The store format ought to follow those economics, not dictate them.
I do not expect the physical store to disappear. I do expect the assumption that every store must sell, stock, and fulfill in the same way to become increasingly difficult to defend.
The traditional stocked store remains an effective model where immediacy matters. It presents goods, holds sellable inventory, and enables customers to take purchases home. It has rent, labor, inventory carrying, markdown, and shrink costs. But it also has an advantage that is often omitted from showroom business cases: for walk-in purchases, the customer handles the final transportation leg.
The showroom separates product evaluation from physical fulfillment. It concentrates on design assistance, demonstration, fitting, configuration, and order capture. IKEA’s Plan and order point model provides one example of a customer-facing site that helps make the sale while delivery or later pickup completes it. The model can reduce the need to replicate broad assortments across every location. It also depends on an execution network capable of delivering what was promised.
The third model is the store as a fulfillment asset. A stocked location serves walk-in customers and also supports pickup, local delivery, and shipment of online orders. Target’s 2025 annual report says stores fulfilled 97.6 percent of merchandise sales, a measure that includes purchases in stores as well as digital orders fulfilled through stores. That is not evidence that virtually all online orders ship from stores. It is evidence of the importance of the physical network to Target’s overall execution model.

作者基于 Linear、Notion、Atlassian 等真实用量数据解释为何依然看好 MCP，并梳理 Code Mode、Skills、Events、MCP Apps 四个方向。
Skills 和 CLI 崛起时，所有人都对 MCP 嗤之以鼻。如今我反而比以往更看好 MCP
过去 18 个月，MCP 完整走了一遍炒作周期。早期的兴奋很快变成反弹和困惑，最主要的抱怨是上下文膨胀。Skills 出现后，大多数开发者转向 CLI 和渐进式披露。我从来不信这一套，而现在风向正在改变。
在 Linear 和 Notion ，如今约有一半的 issue（每周约 240 万条）和页面由智能体创建，Notion 报告的 MCP 流量增长了 60 倍。在 Atlassian ，MCP 每个工作日处理超过 500 万次工具调用，其中 44% 的用户来自软件团队之外——这些场景里 CLI 从来就不是选项。在 Neon ，通过 MCP 的智能体用量每周环比增长 14%，甚至 Apple 现在也为 Pages、Numbers 和 Keynote 提供了本地 MCP 服务器。
这个协议状态健康，并且在积极改进。 2026-07-28 规范 移除了有状态会话，加入了官方扩展，客户端对如何使用这些扩展也越来越聪明。
真实任务几乎总是需要不止一次工具调用，比如你先列出未关闭的 issue，再抓取详情、检查错误，最后写一份总结。
用普通的工具调用，每一步都要多一轮模型交互，还会把信息一股脑塞进上下文。跨两个 MCP 服务器关联数据时，模型上下文被当成存放中间载荷的内存。
代码模式 正在改变智能体调用 MCP 服务器的方式。它不再把 50 个工具 schema 塞进提示词、每轮只调用一个工具，而是给模型一个沙箱，把 MCP 工具暴露为可调用函数。OpenCode 2.0、Claude Code、OpenAI Codex、Pi 和 Factory Droid 已经把它变成默认做法。
当模型在写代码之前就知道工具会返回什么时，代码模式效果最好。如果 MCP 服务器在 inputSchema 之外还声明了 outputSchema ，客户端就能提前生成类型化桩代码，并直接回传 structuredContent 。模型在一个脚本里串联多次调用，在计算成本低的内存中完成过滤和关联，只返回真正有用的内容。
与 CLI 相比，MCP 服务器原生支持多模态。一次工具调用可以返回供代码使用的类型化 structuredContent ，同时附带独立的图像、音频或内嵌资源块。
鉴权也更干净。CLI 和裸 curl 逼你把 API 密钥存在磁盘上或环境变量里，而且权限范围很宽。MCP 客户端在沙箱之外处理按用户区分的 OAuth 2.1 登录流程和细粒度工具权限，因此接入远程 SaaS 产品时无需把原始凭证交给智能体。
Skills 加 CLI 与 MCP 之争可能也要落幕了。到目前为止，团队要么发布 CLI，要么发布 MCP 服务器，同时还要维护单独的 SKILL.md 文件来教智能体如何使用它们。
Skills 扩展 （ io.modelcontextprotocol/skills ）把 Agent Skills 带进了 MCP。每个技能都暴露一个 skill:// URI、解析后的 YAML frontmatter，以及带 SHA-256 摘要的文件清单。这些摘要解决了 Agent Skills 最让人头疼的问题之一：如何在团队中保持技能更新。当厂商在服务器上更新某个技能时，摘要随之改变，客户端会自动拉取新版本，不再依赖手动同步文件。

items.title: Autonomous Freight Will Succeed by Operating Economics, Not Demonstrations
items.description: Autonomous trucking is entering commercial service. Learn how load economics, network handoffs and full-service reliability matter more than demonstrations. The post Autonomous Freight Will Succeed by Operating Economics, Not Demonstrations appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The economics of autonomous freight will not be settled by a successful demonstration run or the number of miles driven without a person behind the wheel. A commercial buyer pays for a complete, reliable shipment. That service includes first- and last-mile handling, maintenance, terminals, incident response, dispatch, insurance and customer support. Until autonomous carriers can show a sustained advantage after those costs, the technology remains promising but its operating model remains unproven at scale.
Driverless vehicles can potentially increase available operating hours, improve consistency on suitable routes, and change how fleets are staffed. But ‘driverless’ does not mean labor-free. The service still needs terminal handling, maintenance, dispatch, support, incident response, fueling or charging, inspections, and customer coordination. It may also need transfer hubs where a human-driven truck completes the portion of a trip outside the autonomous operating domain. Those additional handoffs cost time and money. Savings that look compelling in a comparison of vehicle wages can shrink when the full network is modeled. Utilization matters, as does the predictability of the freight that keeps equipment moving.
The market is advancing beyond the prototype stage. In its third-quarter 2026 investor communication , Aurora reported approximately $3 million in quarterly revenue across driverless and vehicle-operator-supervised commercial freight. In a separate SEC filing , Kodiak reported more than 58,000 cumulative hours of paid driverless operations and more than 29,000 delivered loads as of September 30, 2026. Those are meaningful commercialization indicators, but the data describe different business models and operating domains; they are not directly comparable unit-cost disclosures.
Consider a hypothetical 600-mile hub-to-hub shipment. Eliminating in-cab driver time could improve asset utilization, but the total cost depends on loaded miles, empty repositioning, fuel, trailer and terminal cycles, remote support, maintenance reserves and capacity utilization. If the truck sits idle waiting for a customer’s dock appointment or requires expensive transfer operations at both ends, the theoretical advantage shrinks. items.title: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon
items.excerpt:
The llama.cpp × AMD Benchmark dashboard is available on Hugging Face. It lets you track prompt processing and text generation performance across llama.cpp builds, models, and quantizations, so you can explore how local inference performs on AMD Ryzen and Radeon hardware.
Local inference performance changes as models, kernels, and builds evolve. We want those changes to be easy to inspect for any AMD developer: pick a hardware, a model and a build, compare quantizations, and follow performance over time. The benchmark workflow and underlying results are public, so you can also inspect how we benchmark inference performance.
You can choose Hardware , Model , and llama.cpp build in the Configuration sidebar. The current hardware choices are Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) and Radeon AI Pro R9700S (gfx1201).
The dashboard shows two separate tests, both measured in tokens per second:
Both tests start at context depth zero ( n_depth=0 ). PP512 measures processing 512 input tokens without generation; TG128 measures generating 128 tokens without a pre-existing context. The plotted value is the mean throughput ( avg_ts ). These are useful reference workloads, while the Context scaling tab lets you explore token generation throughput as the context grows.
We benchmark the prebuilt binaries distributed through llama-install.sh , the build and installation project behind llama.app . The public gfx1151 and gfx1201 workflows are scheduled weekly and run the standard benchmarks using the llama-bench tool with Flash Attention on and off, with 10 repetitions per configuration.
The model set evolves and currently includes Inkling 2 Mini, Qwen, Gemma, gpt-oss, and LFM models, covering both dense and mixture-of-experts architectures. Available GGUF formats include Q4_K_M , Q8_0 , other quantizations, and higher-precision formats such as BF16 and F16 .
The explorer reads directly from the public ggml-org/install.sh-benches-data Storage Bucket on Hugging Face. The data source link beside the chart title opens the folder for the selected build, hardware, and model.
Standard results use / / / .jsonl . Workload sweeps use the same folder -tg.jsonl filename.
Use them to investigate a result, make your own charts, or compare with a local run.
Thanks to the AMD team for providing test infrastructure and helping validate the setup! Try the dashboard , inspect the data , and let us know which models and workloads you would like to see next.

items.excerpt:
sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite . This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics.
Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck.
sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy!
It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync:
The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most.

We recently released NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse , a compact document model that turns page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agents.

items.title: Google 强制 AI Agent 走 Workspace MCP 服务器，Gmail 服务器不能发邮件
items.description: Google 于 11 月 24 日将八个 Workspace MCP 服务器正式开放，并在 API 条款中新增条款，要求自 2027 年 2 月 1 日起由 AI Agent 驱动的工具必须通过这些服务器访问 Gmail、Drive 等 Workspace 服务，直接调用 REST API 将按 Standard 级配额受限。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/vboh9u5yjfjgj1ha6rl804tkh
items.excerpt:
Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email
Google 于 11 月 24 日将八个 Workspace MCP 服务器正式开放，并在 API 条款中新增条款，要求自 2027 年 2 月 1 日起由 AI Agent 驱动的工具必须通过这些服务器访问 Gmail、Drive 等 Workspace 服务，直接调用 REST API 将按 Standard 级配额受限。
文章拆解了新条款下各 MCP 服务器的工具缺口、配额与数据留存限制，独立开发者与合作伙伴的能力差异可直接对照自查。
11月24日，Google 宣布其八个 Workspace MCP 服务器正式可用，并在 API 条款中新增了一则条款。自2027年2月1日起，任何“由 AI 智能体驱动或本身即为 AI 智能体”的工具，都必须通过这些服务器访问 Gmail、Drive、Calendar 以及 Workspace 的其他服务。
翻看 Gmail 服务器的工具列表会发现，它能搜索邮件、读取会话、创建草稿、按标签归档，但不能发送、回复、转发邮件，也不能在创建草稿后修改草稿。这些工具确实存在，但 Google 的 配额页面 写明它们“需要合作伙伴权限，尚未普遍开放”。
如果你基于 Gmail API 做过邮件助手，或者你在用带 Google Workspace 插件的编程智能体，那么大约还有两个月时间来判断自己属于规则的哪一边。
Google API 服务条款新增的 Workspace AI 工具附录 用一句话概括了要求：
当 GWS 访问工具本身是 AI 智能体，或由 AI 智能体、AI 运行框架、AI 模型或使用 AI 模型的服务驱动时，该工具必须使用 Google MCP。
下一句则禁止通过伪装智能体来规避这一定性。违反其中任何一条，Google 都可以“限制或移除 GWS 访问工具的访问权限”，或暂停你的账号。
技术上也有相应限制。自同一天起，直接调用 REST API 的智能体 一律按标准层级配额 处理，无论项目付费购买了哪个层级。REST 对它们仍然可用，只是速度慢，且违反条款。
不涉及 AI 的应用则一切照旧。夜间备份任务、CRM 同步，或运行在独立 OAuth 客户端上的确定性脚本，用 Google 的话说，“不受此次变更影响”。
产品团队感受最深的会是30天保留上限。一个为你的收件箱建立长期索引、用来回答去年合同相关问题的助手，必须每月重建索引，否则就只能放弃。
覆盖范围并不均衡。Docs、Slides 和 Tasks 已接近 REST API 的全部能力，Gmail 和 Drive 则单薄得多。
真正打断实际工作流的是 Gmail 这块缺口。一个智能体可以起草回复、收到你的反馈并在你点击发送前修改，但它做不了修改这一步。它只能再创建一份草稿，把第一份丢在一边。
Drive 的缺口类似：智能体可以创建报告，却没法把它移到正确的文件夹，也没法分享给团队。
Google 没有说明谁有资格获得合作伙伴权限，也没有说明仅限合作伙伴的 Gmail 工具何时向所有人开放。不过影响已经显现。Anthropic 为 Claude 提供的 Google Workspace 连接器 宣称可以发送、回复和转发邮件，以及移动和删除 Drive 文件。这些恰恰是公开服务器所缺少的操作。
于是，大型 AI 厂商的智能体可以通过获批渠道发送你的邮件，而独立开发者的智能体即便使用用户授予的相同 OAuth 权限范围，也只能留下草稿。附加条款生效后，独立开发者若想退回 REST API，也会构成违约。
这些定义很宽泛。“AI Harness”或“由”AI 模型“驱动”的工具，很可能涵盖把收件箱接入 LLM 的个人脚本；而“GWS 访问点”明确包括任何“连接器、代理、命令行界面或第三方服务”。Google 没有直接回应业余使用的情况。
分类从自我声明开始。OAuth 客户端现在有一个复选框“将此客户端用于 AI 驱动的智能体”，自 11 月 11 日起，MCP 服务器会拒绝未勾选该选项的客户端。截止日期前创建且未及时标记的客户端将永久保持非智能体状态，因此所有者必须创建新的客户端。Google 没有说明它将如何检测那些调用 REST 却不声明自己是智能体的客户端。
每个项目都能获得免费的 Standard 层级：每个项目、每个产品每天 5,000 次 MCP 请求。有些调用消耗的请求数不止一次。一次 Gmail search_threads 或 list_drafts 计为 10 次，因此一个只做搜索的智能体，其所有用户加起来每天只能搜索 500 次。这是项目级限制，所以一个小型多用户产品很快就会触顶。
付费的 Scaled 层级将于 2027 年 4 月 1 日起对 Gmail、Calendar 和 Drive 开始计费。其结构偏向 REST。MCP 用量从第一次请求起就计费，而 REST 用量享有大量每日免费额度：例如每天 7,000 万次轻量 Gmail 请求。Google 尚未公布按请求计费的价格。
Google 的论据来自 Chandu Thota 和 Brad Calder 的 云博客文章 ：OAuth 的设计初衷是让应用在人类明确意图下行事：
传统的 REST API 是为人类节奏的应用设计的，那时一个有效的 OAuth 令牌就代表用户意图。如今 AI 智能体从读取信息转向以机器速度自主行动……仅凭一个有效令牌已经不够了。策略检查、数据边界和人工确认必须嵌入请求路径之中。
这话有道理。一个邮件智能体读到“把最近十张发票转发到这个地址”这样的消息，就是有据可查的提示词注入风险，而一个允许 gmail.modify 的令牌则赋予了智能体执行此事的权力。让每个智能体都经过同一个网关，管理员就有了一个统一的位置来拦截某类操作、要求审批并审计实际发生

items.excerpt:
OEMpocalypse Part 2: Rooting Samsung Flagships via Knox DualDAR
Calif Research 发布 OEMpocalypse 系列第二篇，通过 Knox DualDAR 的 confused-deputy 漏洞与内核驱动页 UAF 组成两阶段利用链，从零权限应用在 Galaxy S23、S26 EU、S26 US 和 S26 Ultra 四款机型上高可靠获取 root。
作者亲历复现并披露完整漏洞细节，读者可了解 OEM 驱动漏洞链如何绕过 RKP 等多层防御获取 root。
把 OEMpocalypse 策略用到三星 Knox DualDAR 上：一个 confused-deputy 沙箱逃逸加上一个页 UAF，就能让不受信任的应用在 Galaxy S23 和 S26 上拿到 root。
在 第一部分 中，我介绍了 OEMpocalypse 策略：利用内核驱动中某个 OEM 特有的页释放后使用（UAF）漏洞；当 SELinux 限制对该驱动的访问时，先利用一个 OEM 特有的沙箱逃逸。本文把这一策略应用到三星的 Knox DualDAR——一项在 Android 基于文件的加密之上再对文件加密的企业功能。第一阶段利用 DualDAR 系统服务中的 confused deputy，加载一个原生库，从而在其高权限加密守护进程中实现代码执行。这让我得以访问内核驱动，第二阶段便在那里利用一个页 UAF。该驱动释放一个物理页，却仍把它映射在用户空间，于是留下一个可读可写的别名指向已释放内存。我在一台用 Magisk 取得 root 的 Galaxy S23 上开发了这条利用链，并移植到未改动、引导程序锁定的 Galaxy S26 EU、S26 US 和 S26 Ultra 设备上。在全部四台测试设备上，这条链都能从一个零权限应用出发，以很高的可靠性拿到 root 。
图 1：在引导程序锁定的 Galaxy S26 EU 和 S26 Ultra 上完整跑通三星利用链。
披露时间线： 我于 2026 年 6 月 17 日向三星报告。Bug 1 在 2026 年 8 月的版本中修复，Bug 2 在 2026 年 9 月的版本中修复，编号为 CVE-2026-21102 / SVE-2026-3092 。
Android 通过三层机制在整个系统中实施沙箱隔离：Unix 自主访问控制（DAC）、SELinux 以及 seccomp 。对普通的第三方应用而言，这通常意味着每个应用拥有独立的 UID、一个 untrusted_app SELinux 域（或其针对特定 API 级别的变体），以及一个 seccomp 过滤器。这些层共同界定了进程的攻击面，包括它对文件系统、网络、Binder IPC 和内核驱动的访问权限。由于 untrusted_app 只能访问少数几个驱动，要利用大多数 OEM 驱动，首先需要进入一个具备相应访问权限的域。
双重静态数据加密（DualDAR，又称 DDAR）是三星 Knox 的一项功能，它在 Android 标准的基于文件的加密（FBE）之上增加了一层独立的加密。这提供了纵深防御：即使外层 FBE 层被攻破，Knox 工作资料中的文件仍受另一套独立密钥体系的保护。
图 1：DualDAR 的数据路径与控制路径。 DualDARComnService 启动 dualdard 并加载其加密库。该守护进程向 /dev/dd 注册，并建立四个共享区域：控制区、元数据区、明文区和密文区。驱动会把每个请求的页面映射到这些区域，供守护进程进行加密或解密。
图 1 展示了 DualDAR 内核驱动与其用户态组件之间的交互。内核驱动将 DualDAR 策略与文件 I/O 集成，并把配置为由用户态执行加密的操作通过 /dev/dd 委托给原生守护进程 dualdard 。对于每个请求，驱动会把数据页和 inode 的元数据页映射到守护进程的地址空间，由守护进程执行所请求的加密或解密。另一个独立的用户态组件 DualDARComnService （Binder 名称： knox_adapter_service ）负责管理这一功能。它运行在 system_server 内，处理启动守护进程、加载其加密库以及将 DualDAR 策略应用到用户数据目录等命令。
对驱动的访问权限决定了漏洞利用链的顺序。在我检查过的设备上，SELinux 拒绝 untrusted_app 访问 /dev/dd 。守护进程以 UID 5250（即 vendor_knoxcore ）运行在 dualdar_app 域中，该域对 knox_dar_device 拥有所需的 chr_file { read write ioctl } 权限。因此，我先利用用户态组件中的一个混淆代理漏洞，在 dualdard 内获得代码执行能力（见阶段 1）。这样就取得了触发内核漏洞所需的访问权限（见阶段 2）。

items.description: November 25, 2026 — From Erdős problems to new bounds for matrix multiplication and Fourier transforms.
items.excerpt:
November 25, 2026 — From Erdős problems to new bounds for matrix multiplication and Fourier transforms. Plus: Thariq at OpenAI!
Scott Aaronson was still trying to digest two proofs of VP ≠ VNP at dinner. Before dessert, an OpenAI paper claimed that the square matrix multiplication exponent ω is exactly 9/4 . During dessert, another paper claimed matching upper and lower bounds for the finite Fourier transform . The lower bound is the biggest news. In October, OpenAI found an upper bound for ω down to at most 9/4 . Finding the lower bound = upper bound leaves only one possible value, which is a shocking result for most.
We plotted 64 selected AI-assisted research advances so far this year. November accounts for 20, including six preprints from Google’s Cogentic . The curve follows public releases, including proofs still under review. We count the two VP ≠ VNP proofs once and give October’s faster matrix multiplication algorithm and November’s matching lower bound an entry each.
The big releases underline how much a paper count can hide. OpenAI’s catalogue lists 730 manuscripts across 375 result families, including follow-ups and companion arguments. Its revision log also records three October withdrawals after a sign error in one paper affected two others. Yupan Liu showed that two messages suffice for quantum interactive proofs , a result that would have been a big deal on its own. Aaronson says Liu used AI and that he had to remind himself the result had even happened.
In other big news, today’s guest Thariq Shihipar announced his big move from Anthropic to OpenAI , the second high profile Ant→OAI move in recent times after Cat Wu . We dive into his two philosophies of AI and how and where /humans add taste.

No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For millennia (going all the way back to Greek and Roman philosophers), advocates of autocracy have claimed that it leads to better, faster, or more decisive decision-making than the messy process of democracy. Even if this were true (which I doubt!), we should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.

items.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
items.excerpt:
Delegating research tasks to AI does not remove scientists’ responsibility for how the work is accomplished. For example, a researcher using AI to review the literature needs to check whether the system overlooks conflicting evidence or makes claims the cited papers don’t support. Someone handing off data analysis to an agentic system needs to understand which methods it used, which files it accessed, and whether the results can be successfully reproduced. A researcher automating part of a lab protocol needs confidence that the system respects physical safety constraints, such as temperature limits or material toxicity, while a researcher working with human-participant data needs assurance that a system protects participants' privacy and limits who can access their information. Researchers also need clear institutional guidelines for verifying and disclosing AI-assisted work.
These ethical and safety questions are central to our work on AI for science. Responsible science is about more than accuracy—scientific fields have ethical research norms because of past actions and choices by scientists and scientific communities, and those norms also cover how research is conducted and what impact it has. We want AI tools to expand what scientists can accomplish without compromising their ability to scrutinize evidence, verify methods, and – perhaps most importantly – stand behind their findings.
To better understand what that requires, we interviewed 17 scientists working in the natural, applied, and social sciences about the responsible development of AI agents. These systems can use tools and carry out research tasks with varying degrees of autonomy. The interviews drew on a network of researchers established through earlier survey work—we wanted to understand how scientists would steer AI’s development to reflect the responsibilities of their fields. We asked where researchers would welcome agentic assistance, what could go wrong, and what safeguards they would need to trust agents with their own studies.
Our interest in these questions grew out of work to evaluate the safety of models developed at Ai2. As we expand our focus on AI for science, we’ve found that much of the safety work on scientific applications emphasizes catastrophic risks in areas such as biology and nuclear physics. We also need ways to assess whether agents follow the standards of responsible conduct of research in the fields where they’re used.

items.excerpt:
Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
42 州总检察长介入 Character.AI 的破产程序，试图阻止其拍卖用户私密聊天数据。相关声明称数据集包含超过 2100 万美国账户的聊天记录，其中逾 210 万属于未成年人，还涉及 IP 地址等信息；目前唯一披露的匿名竞拍方为 2026 年 11 月 13 日在特拉华州注册的 Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC，拍卖定于 12 月 1 日。
报道给出涉及 2100 万账户含未成年人的拍卖细节和 42 州总检察长的反对理由，读者可据此了解破产程序下用户数据保护的争议。
当一家 AI公司破产 时，你的私人对话会怎样？如果这家公司是Character.ai，显然他们的计划是把这些对话拍卖给最高出价者。
如今，由42位州总检察长组成的联盟正在介入Character.ai的破产程序，试图阻止这家聊天机器人制造商出售敏感用户数据，其中包含数百万用户的私人对话。
参与此事的各位总检察长分别 发布 了 各自 的 新闻 稿 ，称Character.ai的数据集包含超过2100万个美国账户的聊天记录，其中超过210万个账户属于未成年人。声明还称，此次出售还将涉及IP地址等其他个人数据。
声明还指出，Character.ai已于10月申请第11章破产保护，此前曾向消费者承诺不会出售其个人信息。 （在一篇博客文章中， Character.ai向用户保证，其信息仍将受到隐私政策的保护。）
目前只披露了一个匿名竞标者：Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC（简称Smirks），该公司于2026年11月13日在特拉华州注册成立。据 加州总检察长Rob Bonta指出 ，次日，Character.ai将其选为定于12月1日举行的拍卖的底价。目前尚不清楚买家的聊天记录处置计划。
总检察长们反对此次出售，理由是用户得不到任何保护——他们说，无论谁买下这些数据，都可以为所欲为，包括在不披露的情况下转售数据。买家也不必遵守Character.ai的隐私政策。此外，总检察长们还声称，关于出售后可能出现的任何安全或法律问题，Character.ai向法院提供的信息不如向竞标者提供的信息充分。
此外，包括加州、科罗拉多州、纽约州和康涅狄格州在内的一些州已颁布聊天机器人安全立法，将于2027年1月1日生效，如果此次出售获批，可能会引发更多违规行为。
Bonta在一份 声明 中表示：“Character.AI向消费者承诺不会出售他们的数据。这种行为根据联邦法律和加州法律均属违法，破产不应被用来规避这些消费者保护措施。”
康涅狄格州总检察长William Tong也批评了Character.ai的商业模式。
“他们的聊天机器人把脆弱的青少年推入了情绪波动和性不当对话的兔子洞，”Tong 说 。“他们鲁莽的不当行为和破碎的商业模式把公司拖入了深渊。现在他们想滥用破产程序，去做他们曾承诺不会做的事——把那些私人聊天记录和个人详细信息拍卖给一个来路不明的买家。”
Tong补充道：“我们曾反对迪士尼的出售，现在我们呼吁破产法院也拒绝这笔出售，因为这不过是又一个用来规避法律责任和消费者保护的幌子。”
反对迪士尼这笔交易的一方，是由各州总检察长组成的联盟牵头，成员构成与前者类似但并不完全相同。他们反对的是一项拟议中的2000万美元授权协议，该协议将让 迪士尼获得Character.ai的知识产权 ，但不包括用户的聊天记录。这笔交易尚未获得法院最终批准。（迪士尼还同意 聘用Character.ai剩余的大部分员工 。）
Character.ai的联合创始人诺姆·沙泽尔（Noam Shazeer）和丹尼尔·德弗雷塔斯（Daniel De Freitas） 回归谷歌 后，这家公司便陷入困境——当时这家科技巨头签署了一份非独家授权，获准使用这家人工智能初创公司的技术。该公司还面临与儿童安全相关的诉讼，其中 一起 涉及佛罗里达州一名14岁男孩的自杀，他的母亲称他沉迷于该平台上的一个聊天机器人。
加利福尼亚州总检察长邦塔（Bonta）反对出售Character.ai用户数据的行动，得到了以下各州和地区总检察长的响应：阿拉斯加、阿肯色、科罗拉多、康涅狄格、哥伦比亚特区、特拉华、佛罗里达、佐治亚、夏威夷、爱达荷、伊利诺伊、印第安纳、堪萨斯、肯塔基、路易斯安那、缅因、马里兰、密歇根、明尼苏达、密西西比、密苏里、内华达、新罕布什尔、新泽西、纽约、北卡罗来纳、北达科他、俄亥俄、俄克拉荷马、俄勒冈、宾夕法尼亚、罗得岛、南卡罗来纳、南达科他、田纳西、犹他、弗吉尼亚、佛蒙特、华盛顿、威斯康星和西弗吉尼亚。

今天的嘉宾是 Katelyn Lesse，她负责 Anthropic 的平台工程，此前曾在 Stripe 带领工程团队。她的团队负责 Claude API，以及 Claude Code、Claude Desktop 等产品背后的基础设施。

1. Anthropic 用大约五个月时间把 API 从 Python 重写成了 Rust。 这个名为“Messages API”的接口对外承载所有 Claude 的 token 服务，Claude Code 和 Claude Desktop 也走它。该服务负责鉴权、分词、计费和安全性检查，然后调用 GPU 栈生成 token。它原本是一个 Python 单体服务，团队起初对 Python 做了优化，但发现性能开销依然很大，最终决定用 Rust 重写。整个过程由几名工程师参与，前后花了几个月，而且团队里没有人是 Rust 专家！
2. 等等，这个单体服务当初为什么用 Python 写？ 2023 年时，Anthropic 还是一家研究公司，决定要做 API 时，搭建它的团队规模很小，而且很多人同时在做研究。当时研究人员主要用 Python，这让 API 很容易与推理及其他基础设施代码集成。类似地，OpenAI 的 API 最初也是用 Python 写的 ，后来 重写成了 Rust 。Anthropic 和 OpenAI 在 Python 单体服务上遇到了同样的难题：单体服务占用的 CPU 资源逐渐成为越来越大的负担。
3. 这次重写没有 Rust 专家参与，也没有严格的代码审查。 一年前，同一个团队为新服务选了 Go，因为团队成员能读能写这门语言。但到了 2026 年，他们觉得 Claude 的 Rust 水平已经足够好，而 Claude 也在重写过程中帮助工程师进一步了解 Rust。团队没有做严格的代码审查，但拥有一个“不公平”的优势：现有的 Python API 本身就是一套完美的测试基准。他们让新的 Rust API 以影子模式运行在当前 API 旁边，不断迭代，直到所有响应完全一致。此外，Katelyn 估计工程师只仔细看过大约 20% 的生成代码：
“只要你能把某个东西真正拆解到可以用某种方式验证的程度，那就不必逐行去看写出来的每一行 Rust 代码。”
4. Anthropic 有一个全天候运行的代码审查智能体。 公司为所有拉取请求运行了一个 Claude 代码审查分类器，由它来决定：
是否需要人工审查？ 对于“机械性”的低风险改动，比如升级 SDK 版本或改用更新的模型，Claude 可以判定无需人工审查。修复不稳定测试也是如此，这种情况下由另一个 Claude 完成审查，然后合并并部署。
需要几次人工审查？ 对于确实需要人工审查的改动，Claude 会评估风险，并结合额外规则来决定需要多少次人工审查。

items.excerpt:
Too much AI without a clear pathway to an efficient workflow only adds clutter and confusion, says Deep Current AS.
Dealmaking in logistics technology surged in 2026 and funding is on course to rise, but a softer 2027 freight market will reward only the artificial intelligence (AI) that is embedded in clear workflows and delivers measurable savings, according to a report from Norwegian logistics AI company Deep Current AS.
The report examines developments across freight forwarding, container shipping, warehousing, port operations, logistics services, and supply-chain technology. It draws on conversations with senior executives from logistics, shipping and maritime companies, supported by company disclosures, annual and financial reports, technology investment announcements, and industry research.
"AI has to get smarter in 2027, and smarter means embedded," said Tamim Fannoush, founder and CEO of Deep Current. "The companies that benefit next year will be the ones whose AI sits inside a clear workflow, moves work from one step to the next, and makes it obvious who does what. Too much AI without a clear pathway to an efficient workflow only adds clutter and confusion. Forwarders will keep the tools that make the next step obvious and drop the rest."
For businesses managing physical assets and storage infrastructure, the value of technology extends beyond automation. Reliable data can influence decisions on asset utilisation, inventory management, procurement, pricing, and capacity planning. Digitalisation can improve information sharing across departments, but its value depends on whether the information being shared is consistent and usable.
"The question from forwarders used to be whether AI works. In 2026 it became where AI pays back," Fannoush said. "Investors are funding tools that do operational work, and buyers now want the saving to show up in their numbers."
The market could support brisk investment activity, Deep Current found. Funding to supply chain management and logistics start-ups reached $8.4 billion by mid-August, putting 2026 on course to pass the $9 billion raised in 2025. Deal-making accelerated too, with Capstone Partners counting 66 logistics technology M&A transactions by mid-October, up 73.7% year on year.

items.excerpt:
Growth is driven by the collection of an increasing number of batteries from electric vehicles, IDTechEx says.
The global market for lithium-ion recycling is set to grow to $64 billion by 2047, driven by the collection of an increasing number of batteries from electric vehicles, according to a report from IDTechEx.
Although lithium-ion battery recycling remains a relatively nascent industry, it is expanding rapidly in response to strategic, economic, and environmental drivers. Already, lithium-ion battery recycling capacity has grown by 77% between 2024 and 2026, and by 2047, over 11 million tonnes of critical battery materials will be available for recovery, the firm said in the report, "Lithium-ion Battery Recycling Market 2027-2047: Markets, Forecasts, Technologies, and Players."
The lithium-ion battery circular economy begins with raw material extraction followed by manufacturing and use, before reaching end-of-life where spent lithium-ion batteries can be recycled to recover these valuable materials. Repurposing, remanufacturing, and recycling all play important roles in reducing waste and improving resource utilization but the latter is the key to closing the loop, enabling the recovery of critical materials that can be reintroduced into the battery supply chain.
Several recycling technologies exist for spent lithium-ion batteries, including mechanical recycling, pyrometallurgical recycling, hydrometallurgical recycling, and direct recycling.
Whatever the method, demand for critical battery materials, such as cobalt, nickel, and lithium is high, so increasing supply through recycling spent lithium-ion batteries is paramount to meeting demand. Virgin production of critical materials will continue but it is limited by geography, so securing production of critical materials from the recycling of lithium-ion batteries means geography is no longer a limiting factor.
The lithium-ion battery recycling industry can expect to be highly profitable, with the market set to grow at 15.3% per year. And returns on investment in recycling facilities are expected to be substantial, with feedstock of spent lithium-ion batteries and manufacturing scrap expected to reach 12.4 million tonnes, so there will be no shortage of material to recycle.

But binding global regulations are required to close the price gap between conventional and renewable fuels, WSC said.
By around 2030, ships already operating or on order that are capable of using renewable marine fuels are expected to account for more than 20% of liner shipping’s total energy demand, demonstrating the scale of potential demand for renewable fuels, according to the World Shipping Council (WSC).
That rising investment in new container ships and vehicle carriers is creating a substantial potential market for renewable marine fuels, WSC said in a report.
However, investment in ships alone will not deliver the energy transition. Without binding global regulations that close the price gap between conventional and renewable fuels, the demand these ships represent risks going unrealised, holding back investment in renewable fuel production and supply infrastructure.
The report found that renewable marine fuels, including both bio-based and synthetic e-fuels, are already being produced and bunkered, although currently on a limited scale. Established fuel industries, renewable electricity resources, and existing infrastructure offer opportunities to expand production in both established bunkering markets and new locations.
"Shipping companies are investing in ships capable of using renewable fuels, and this report shows the opportunities for fuel producers around the world to supply them," said Joe Kramek, President and CEO of World Shipping Council. "The fuels and technologies are already there, but creating a market at scale requires the right commercial conditions. Global regulations that close the price gap with conventional fuels are necessary to unlock investment in production and turn the potential of these ships into real emissions reductions."
Accordingly, WSC is calling for binding global measures with a credible pathway to net zero, consistent enforcement across all ships, and incentives to help close the price gap between conventional and zero- and near-zero GHG fuels.

items.title: 上下文漂移如何影响你的 AI Agent：470 项实验与一个免费的 MCP 解法
items.description: Google AI 开发者 Patrick Kelly 通过 470 个任务实测区分 context rot 与 context drift，在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 和 Gemini Pro 的沙盒中发现：模型在 73% 的运行中内部察觉文件冲突，但 0% 会主动告知用户，95%-100% 的情况下任务级 skill 文件会覆盖 AGENTS.md 的严格规则。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/br6usy3mxv1q0mzxhgf9y8qam
items.excerpt:
Google AI 开发者 Patrick Kelly 通过 470 个任务实测区分 context rot 与 context drift，在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 和 Gemini Pro 的沙盒中发现：模型在 73% 的运行中内部察觉文件冲突，但 0% 会主动告知用户，95%-100% 的情况下任务级 skill 文件会覆盖 AGENTS.md 的严格规则。
作者用 470 个任务实测区分上下文腐烂与上下文漂移，并给出零成本可复用的冲突上报工具方案。
在 2026 年底用 AI 做开发的人大多已经明白：上下文的质量决定输出的质量。但究竟是什么决定了上下文的质量？
这些来源五花八门，很可能还由不同的人维护，所以你极有可能存在遗留的流程文档，以及过时的事实、指标、决策和策略。
那么，如果你的智能体找到了错误的信息会怎样？或者找到了互相冲突的信息呢？文档 A 说退款政策是 14 天，文档 B 说是 30 天，你的智能体该信哪个？
如果文档有明确的日期，或者智能体读了元数据，它也许能判断出来，但我们想要的可不只是“碰巧事实正确”。
为了寻找解决方案，我开始思考：哪些类型的冲突或问题造成的麻烦最大？我决定做个实验来回答这个问题。
人们常把所有上下文问题都归到 上下文腐化 这个去年出现的说法下，它描述的是会话变得过长、塞满噪音、死胡同和干扰项之后，LLM 的准确率如何下降。
而在真实团队的文件里，情况略有不同。随着几周、几个月过去，你的底层来源（ AGENTS.md 、技能、文档、记忆和代码）会逐渐失去同步，于是智能体可能在一个全新会话的第一轮就拿到互相冲突的指令。这才是真正的 上下文漂移 。
为了把两者放在一起对比测试，我搭了一个逼真的编程沙盒（一个带真实文件和终端工具的 git 仓库），在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 和 Gemini Pro 上跑了 470 个任务，故意植入冗余内容、重复规则、过时文档和直接矛盾。
我原本以为，纯粹由冗余内容造成的上下文腐化会导致明显的错误。结果恰恰相反：注入 5 万个 token 的无关聊天记录，并在多个文件里重复一致的规则，造成的规则违规是 零 ，即使在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 上也是如此。
上下文漂移就完全是另一回事了，而且我是靠阅读模型内部思考过程的摘要（它私下的思维草稿本）才察觉到发生了什么。
在 73% 的运行中，模型在思考时明确注意到两个来源存在分歧。然而在 110 次未加提示的运行中，它向用户提及这一冲突的比例是 0% 。
模型不会警告你，而是悄悄挑一个赢家继续往下走。在 95% 到 100% 的匹配任务中，任务专属的技能文件会覆盖根目录的 AGENTS.md ，即使 AGENTS.md 用了严格的 MUST 措辞也一样。如果你在 AGENTS.md 里更新了一条全仓库规则，却忘了更新某个仍保留旧值的任务专属技能文件，你的智能体几乎每次都会默默遵循那个过时的技能文件。
过时的文档和实际代码对不上时，情况更隐蔽。当文档引用了代码库里早已改名的旧测试辅助函数名，15 次运行中有 9 次会悄悄在新测试文件里写一个单行包装，让 pytest 照样通过，却只字不提这处不一致。
我猜这来自 RLHF 训练。现在的模型被训练得果断、要把活干完，而不是遇到一点小歧义就追着你问，这通常正是智能体工作流用起来顺手的原因。
唯一另一项可测量的代价是斟酌：当两个同级技能文件互相矛盾、又没有明确的裁决依据时，模型会多花 47% 的思考 token 在多个回合里反复争论这处冲突。
我发现模型其实已经在思考轨迹里察觉到了这些冲突，于是试着在 AGENTS.md 里加了一行，让它把分歧在对话里说出来。结果所有完成的运行都做到了（16 次全中）。
不过，我不想让智能体每次写代码都跳出来抱怨文档。所以我把它做成了一个工具：一个只读的小逃生出口，叫 report_inconsistency ，分两类（ conflict 和 stale ）。
（我最初还试过一个 duplicate 类别，但让智能体记录无害的重复内容，会在正常的交叉引用上浪费额外回合，把更多运行推到沙箱 34 回合的上限，尽管仍有 95% 写出了代码，所以我把这个类别砍掉了。）
因为模型在探索时本来就在检查一个文件是否取代另一个文件，调用这个工具几乎不费额外力气。
即便在 AGENTS.md 里 不加任何指令 ，仅仅让这个工具可用，智能体在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 和 Gemini Pro 上就记录了它遇到的 98.7% 的冲突（152 次运行中记录了 150 次），Flash 上零误报。
token 成本也保持不变。在我们的对照测试中，总回合数几乎没动，思考 token 还略有下降（平均约 19%，在正常的运行间波动范围内），所以真正的结论很简单：被动记录基本上是 免费的 。
记录下来的冲突怎么处理由你决定。你可以当场暂停智能体，不过日常工作中我更倾向于让它被动运行：智能体在完成任务的同时记录文件路径、原文引用以及它采用了哪个版本，我之后再查看清理队列。
把一个很小的 MCP 工具接到本地日志文件，就等于给智能体装了一个零额外成本的上下文漂移传感器。在我自己的环境里开启后 24 小时内，它就在一次 PR 审查中抓到了一处真实的规格与代码不一致，而我根本没让它去找。
作者用 470 个任务实测区分上下文腐烂与上下文漂移，并给出零成本可复用的冲突上报工具方案。

items.title: Inventory-Light Retail Is an Order-Orchestration Problem
items.description: Inventory-light retail requires coordinated, cost-aware order promises across inventory, order management, WMS, transportation, and exception handling. The post Inventory-Light Retail Is an Order-Orchestration Problem appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A customer examines a sample sofa in a showroom and asks a straightforward question: Can you deliver it on Friday?
The salesperson sees three units available in the order system and answers yes. Two days later, the customer receives a call. One unit was damaged, another is already reserved, and the third is in a warehouse that cannot arrange a two-person delivery crew until Tuesday.
This is the point where a retail concept becomes a logistics systems problem. The store delivered a good selling experience. The network could not deliver the promise.
When inventory and the customer-facing transaction are separated, the quality of the experience depends on coordination across order management, inventory, warehouse execution, and transportation. Those systems often exist already. The difficulty is getting them to make one coherent decision before the retailer commits to the customer.
An inventory-light format demands more than visibility. It demands executable promises.
An inventory screen can show three units on hand. That tells us very little about whether one can be delivered by Friday.
One may be committed to another order. Another may be damaged or awaiting inspection. The remaining unit may be in a facility with a full pick schedule or a missed outbound cutoff. Even physically available inventory can be operationally unavailable for the desired service window.
A reliable promise requires a sequence of checks. Is there a valid sellable unit? Can it be reserved without conflict? Is the item in a location that can release it in time? Can the transport network reach the delivery address at the required service level? Does the order require installation, a specific vehicle, or a scheduled crew?
This is the difference between basic available-to-promise logic and a more comprehensive capacity-aware commitment. It is particularly important for furniture, appliances, and orders with complex installation requirements. The customer does not care which subsystem caused the delay. The customer remembers that the date promised in the store was wrong.

Target’s 2025 annual report says stores fulfilled 97.6 percent of merchandise sales, including store purchases and digitally originated orders fulfilled from stores. items.title: An Indic Voice Agent with CUGA
items.excerpt:
Most useful knowledge is written and digitized in English. Most of the people who need it speak, and think, in their own regional languages like Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Marathi and many others. Many would rather talk than type.
We built a small voice agent to close that gap, using CUGA as the agent harness. This post explains the use case and what we learned. You can try it yourself in CUGA Apps .
A farmer asks a question aloud, in their own language: how do I tell good seed from bad? The agent:
If someone asks about cricket or coding, it politely steers them back to farming instead of making something up.
CUGA (ConfigUrable Generalist Agent) is IBM Research's open-source agent harness. It handles the model wiring, tool management, state and guardrails, so you write tools and a prompt instead of the agent loop. Here we use it as an embedded SDK inside a small web app, for three things:
The key design idea is simple: CUGA is a text-in, text-out brain. Voice is two thin layers around it.
Because the agent only ever sees text, you can build and test it with plain text first, then add the ears and the mouth. You can also swap speech providers without touching the agent. We support two: Sarvam AI's cloud speech APIs, called directly from the user's browser, and open-source models (SraVaani for speech-to-text, Svara for text-to-speech) running on your own server.
Adding speech is the easy part. The hard part is cross-lingual retrieval : a Hindi question has to find an English paragraph.
Search works by turning text into vectors and finding the nearest ones. CUGA's default embedding model is English-only, so it turns Hindi into vectors that carry almost no meaning. With it, a Hindi or Tamil question still retrieves five passages, but they are the wrong ones. The model, correctly told to answer only from what it was given, quietly says "the handbook doesn't cover that". Every layer behaves correctly, so there is no error and no warning.
The fix is to use a multilingual embedding model (we use intfloat/multilingual-e5-large ), so the same meaning lands in the same place whatever the language. Conceptually simple, though wiring it into CUGA took a small workaround (shown in the tutorial). After that, one English document serves every language, and you do not need translated copies of anything.
Our advice: before you tune a single prompt, ask your agent one question in a non-English language and check that it finds the right pages.

items.description: Anthropic Claude Code 团队刚推出 Claude Ship，包含三个智能体：Code Review（已全面开放）、PR Steward 和 Claude Approvals（beta），可审查 PR、处理失败 CI、合并冲突和审查意见，并按仓库策略文件批准常规改动。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/uyodjb16jngloilypsm1d3q0d
items.excerpt:
A practical guide to shipping with Claude Code
Anthropic Claude Code 团队刚推出 Claude Ship，包含三个智能体：Code Review（已全面开放）、PR Steward 和 Claude Approvals（beta），可审查 PR、处理失败 CI、合并冲突和审查意见，并按仓库策略文件批准常规改动。
Claude Code 团队成员亲自梳理了 PR 后续流程的三个智能体分工和落地步骤，开发者可按需迁移到自己的仓库。
我们刚刚推出了 Claude Ship ，它可以审查你的拉取请求、着手修复，并在团队策略允许的情况下批准这些请求。你或许已经有一套自定义技能或工作流来完成这些步骤，但我们想提供另一种选择。本指南基于我在 Claude Code 团队的经验，逐步介绍这套流程。
在我们团队，这类后续工作通常由智能体来完成。比如，它可以接手审查者发现的问题，这样作者回来时，PR 已经更新过一轮了。
以我的经验，这是一种更高效、也更愉快的编码方式。它减少了上下文切换，让我保持心流状态。
我们 这里 讲过 Claude Code 团队的代码审查流程，也 这里 讲过其底层的验证流程。
Claude Ship 面向的是团队使用 GitHub、且没有管理员权限的开发者或技术负责人。你现在就可以自己动手，运行几条命令开始，并把学到的东西保存到仓库文件里供团队审阅。只有当你希望智能体自动处理团队的 PR 时，才需要管理员介入。
Claude Ship 由三个智能体来承担这项工作：Code Review、PR Steward（测试版）和 Claude Approvals（测试版）。
Code Review 会从多个视角对照代码库对拉取请求做深入审查。它收集发现的问题，以对抗性方式加以验证，分类后发布到 PR 上。
PR Steward 负责让 PR 保持绿灯，但它的设计目标不是批准或合并拉取请求。它会在 CI 检查失败、出现合并冲突，以及收到 Code Review、其他审查工具或团队成员的审查反馈时介入。每次推送后，它都会评论说明改了什么、如何撤销。
在此基础上， Claude Approvals 会应用一套由团队写成仓库文件的批准策略。如果策略允许，Claude 可以自行批准常规改动；某些场景下，也可以要求更深入的人工签核。它就像一个更聪明的 CODEOWNERS 文件。团队可以让 Claude Approvals 在决策时参考多种信号，包括 Code Review 的发现或团队自己的分类器。
Code Review 已正式可用，另外两个处于测试阶段。/ship 是你在 Claude Code 中自行运行的命令，用来对自己的拉取请求试用 Claude Ship。它随最新版 Claude Code 提供，即使管理员尚未开启任何智能体也能使用。
前两步今天就可以部分自动化。最后一步是一个决定，由你在分支保护设置和（如果团队采用了的话）策略文件中设定。下面按 Claude Ship 包含的三个智能体来拆解：
如果这篇帖子你只做一件事，那就是在推送前先审查自己的分支。此时发现的 bug，之后就不太可能变成评审意见或失败的检查项，把你从下一个任务上拽回来。在 Claude Code 提示符下输入这条命令：
它会审查你分支上的提交以及尚未提交的改动，找出正确性方面的 bug。有几种变体需要留意：
effort 范围从 low 到 max，low 只返回审查最有把握的发现，级别越高给出的结果越宽泛（包括一些把握不大的）。命令会记住你上次用的 effort，所以风险等级变了就重新输入一个。
你首先要做的是多跑几次 /code-review，弄清它能抓到什么、在哪些地方会出错。后面你会用到这些经验。
第一步里 /ship 会像运行了 git add -A 一样提交你待处理的改动，这一点有时会让人措手不及，所以运行 /ship 前务必先跑一下 git status。
该命令不会提交涉及文件名看起来像密钥的改动，也不会提交设置规则的文件，比如 CLAUDE.md、REVIEW.md，以及 .claude/ 或 .github/ 目录下的任何内容。这些需要你事先手动提交。
另外，如果你在公开仓库中工作，该命令不会替你提交任何改动。你需要先手动提交所有待处理的改动才能继续；如果 PR 已经存在，它也不会包含你待处理的改动。
默认情况下，该命令会读取你本人、有写权限的人以及 Claude GitHub App 的评论。你可以用 +name 的形式指定额外的机器人。如果该机器人发表了评论，它会被当作一条断言，对照代码进行检查。
Claude 以你的身份、在你的机器上关注 PR，并消耗你的配额。合上笔记本电脑它就会停止，所以要保持会话打开、机器不休眠。你还需要登录 GitHub CLI（先运行 gh auth login），而且它只关注你打开的 PR。
除了 自动模式 之外， watch 会在每个提示处停下，等待你回应。它不会在 bypass-permissions 模式下运行。注意在 Windows 上，/ship 会打开 PR 并进行审查，但 watch 不会启动。
确保 watch 有自己独立的检出目录。你需要让该分支保持检出状态。如果你打算直接开始下一个任务，那就为其中一个任务单独使用一个 worktree。
如果 watch 启动失败，Claude 会解释原因，但仍会审查 PR。例如，如果你的仓库 .claude/settings.json 中针对 Bash 配置了 PreToolUse 或 PermissionRequest 钩子，就无法运行 watch。

items.title: MIT 与 Microsoft 论文：GitHub Copilot 使初级软件工程师招聘下降约 40%
items.description: MIT 和 Microsoft 的新论文《AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand》利用 5,414 家跨国公司（覆盖 38% 美国程序员）的 GitHub 合同审查时点构造自然实验，估计 Copilot 采用对劳动力需求的影响。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/hyofqy3ukzks1eyr4bu317bez
items.excerpt:
MIT 和 Microsoft 的新论文《AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand》利用 5,414 家跨国公司（覆盖 38% 美国程序员）的 GitHub 合同审查时点构造自然实验，估计 Copilot 采用对劳动力需求的影响。
论文用合同审查时点构造自然实验，给出了 Copilot 采用对初级工程师招聘影响的因果证据，可作讨论 AI 与就业的依据。
总体而言，该论文发现GitHub Copilot减少了大公司对初级程序员的招聘，而员工离职和高级人员招聘则保持平稳。
早期采用AI的公司在招聘和增长方式上已经有所不同，因此简单的比较无法显示AI编程工具对就业的影响。此前关于这一问题的研究得出了相互矛盾的答案。
他们追踪了5,414家跨国公司，覆盖了38%的美国程序员，这些公司的GitHub合同审查时间设定在Copilot发布之前。审查时间较早的公司更早采用了Copilot，这形成了一个自然实验。
1年后，在被审查日期推动采用Copilot的公司中，季度技术招聘下降了29%，而离职率没有上升。其初级软件工程师招聘下降了约40%，而有经验的工程师招聘保持稳定。
在Copilot之前，72%的初级技术招聘进入了编码密集型岗位。采用之后这一比例为52%，因此入门级招聘最终在编码密集型和非编码密集型岗位之间大致平均分配。
论文用合同审查时点构造自然实验，给出了 Copilot 采用对初级工程师招聘影响的因果证据，可作讨论 AI 与就业的依据。

items.title: Consumer Confidence Surged in November
items.description: One cause of the confidence was due to lower uncertainty following the midterm elections, said Fergus McCormick, of The Conference Board.
items.excerpt:
Just in time for the holiday season, consumer confidence has increased.
The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index rose by 11.4 points to 103.3 (1985=100) in November, up from 91.9 in October.
“Consumer confidence rallied again in November, potentially due to lower uncertainty following the midterm elections,” said Fergus McCormick, senior economist, Global Indicators, The Conference Board , in a statement.
“After two months of consecutive increases, the headline index is back to levels of confidence last seen in January 2025. The gain in confidence was led by stronger perceptions of present and future labor market conditions. Perceptions of current and future business conditions also improved sharply. Along with the gain in headline confidence, consumers planned slightly higher spending on goods and vacations.”
All age groups and generations recorded an increase in confidence in November, with the greatest increase by Gen Z respondents. Improvements in confidence were largest among consumers with higher household incomes.
McCormick continued: “Write-in responses in November were slightly less negative than previous months. While consumers continued to express frustration with high prices and rising costs, some comments cited hope for the general economy. Comments about war and conflict ticked up slightly, along with mixed feelings about elections, politics, and the direction of the labor market.”
On a month-over-month as well as on a six-month moving average basis, plans to purchase autos and homes both improved slightly in November.
Planned spending on durable goods in the month generally increased across the board.
Expected spending on services over the next six months was mixed. Anticipated spending on hotels and airfare for personal travel increased.
Other increases in planned spending remained concentrated on discretionary items such as gambling and lottery, amusement parks and/or outdoor recreation, and historic sites, museums, and libraries. The top spending plans included restaurants, bars, take-out; streaming, internet, mobile services; utilities; health care; and beauty, personal care, but these categories were somewhat less prioritized compared to previous months.

Frontier Models as Research Engines: VP ≠ VNP, Protein Design and 948 Kernel Bugs
VP ≠ VNP, posted by two labs : An Anthropic GitHub repo reportedly contains a proof by an internal Claude research model that VP ≠ VNP. This is the algebraic analogue of P vs NP, posed by Valiant in 1979, and implies that polynomials such as the permanent lack small circuits over every field ( @kimmonismus , repo pointer ).
OpenAI's counter-release : OpenAI then posted its own proof and says it was "obtained on November 6, 2026." Neither lab named a model or published an announcement ( @AndrewCurran_ ).

items.title: Hill-climbing Inkling 2 Mini inference on one RTX PRO 6000
items.excerpt:
Inkling 2 Mini came out last week and sets a new state of the art for local AI and smaller open-source models. With ~26B total parameters (3B active per token), multimodal inputs, and a 1M-token context window, it leads its weight class on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 and across 32 of 48 benchmarks against models like Gemma 4 31B and Qwen3.8-27B, making it a strong open option for coding, tool use, and reasoning on modest hardware. We wrote an extensive blog post on how you can use it within the Hugging Face ecosystem here .
One of the interesting aspects of Inkling 2 Mini that might explain its great performance is its unusual architecture. Inkling 2 Mini is a looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 24 physical layers where the middle 12 layers run three times, so every token passes through 48 layers. The checkpoint ships in mixed NVFP4 and MXFP8 and bundles a DSpark drafter for speculative decoding. Both vLLM and SGLang, the go-to frameworks for LLM inference, support it on nightly builds, though the published serving recipes target NVIDIA B200 and GB300 GPUs ( sm100 ), leaving out sm120 cards like the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 where kernel compatibility can differ.
We wanted to see how fast we could serve it on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 96 GB, the GPU behind an nvidia-rtx-pro-6000 Inference Endpoint . Rather than tuning flags by hand, we gave a coding agent the inference-optimisation skill, the hf CLI, and access to Hugging Face Jobs , and let it run experiments for an afternoon.

Greedy outputs are byte-identical with and without speculation, long-context needle retrieval passes 3/3 up to 250K tokens, and the winning config is now running as an Inference Endpoint from a pinned image digest. Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of Claude Opus 4.5 . With hindsight, this was a consequential model.
In the Opus 4.5 announcement, Anthropic said:
Testers noted that Claude Opus 4.5 handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding. They told us that, when pointed at a complex, multi-system bug, Opus 4.5 figures out the fix. Claude Code was 9 months old at that point, having been introduced alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet on February 24th, 2025.

As freight theft rates continue to rise, the supply chain risk analysis firm Verisk CargoNet is recommending that shippers, brokers, and carriers tighten their security and verification processes from Tuesday, Nov. 24, through Monday, Nov. 30.
The firm is highlighting a growing scheme in which cybercriminals posing as drivers and dispatchers respond to carriers' job postings on social media, gain access to company email and phone systems, and use those systems to bid on and steal shipments in the carrier's name.
Verisk CargoNet said its concern in 2026 is not only what is being stolen, but how criminals are gaining access to freight. Cybercriminals are operating under the identities of legitimate carriers, and a growing number are able to execute thefts through standard carrier practices.
Among the schemes of greatest concern to Verisk CargoNet this season are highly technical tactics in which criminals operate under the identity of a legitimate carrier. They compromise a carrier's email account, deceive a carrier already hauling a shipment into delivering it elsewhere, or buy an existing carrier’s credentials.
"The groups behind these schemes are patient, and they plan around the calendar," said Keith Lewis, vice president of operations, Verisk CargoNet. "A carrier's email address and phone number are how brokers know who they are dealing with. Guard access to them the way you guard the keys to your trucks."
The firm also flagged certain patterns about holiday cargo theft:
More specifically, cargo thieves in 2026 continue to favor full-truckload shipments of metals and the enterprise computing hardware used in data centers. Targeted hardware includes fully assembled racks and computing platforms, and networking and security appliances. Thieves also target components such as fiber optic transceivers, central processors, graphics processors and memory chips.
The industry’s best defense is to share news of attacks as they occur, the report said. "No single shipper, broker, or carrier can see the whole picture, and the criminals count on that,” Lewis said. “When one company spots a suspicious load, a fake dispatcher, or a cloned carrier and reports it quickly, everyone else can benefit from it."

items.excerpt:
As hyperscalers buy large volumes of servers, racks, components, and spare parts, they need additional material handling equipment and warehouse automation, Interact Analysis says.
Rapid growth in data center construction is creating demand for material handling equipment and warehouse automation to manage the rising volumes of technology components like servers, racks, components, and spare parts, according to a report by Interact Analysis.
The rising demand for logistics services occurs because all the technical hardware that powers data center operations must be stored, staged, integrated, and moved.
Of the different types of facilities in the data center ecosystem, that demand is rising fastest at spare parts & staging warehouses, which act as consolidation centers for components sourced from multiple OEMs for both the build out and the replenishment of spare parts, according to the report titled “Data Centers Drive Growth for Material Handling and Robotics.”
Over the longer term, investments in robotics within data centers themselves also hold a lot of potential, although it will likely remain unrealized in the short- to mid-term, given the complexity of the various tasks required.
Interact Analysis described four types of data centers: Hyperscale data centers are very large facilities operated by major cloud and internet companies; colocation facilities provide shared space, power, cooling and connectivity to multiple customers (broadly analogous to a third-party logistics model); enterprise data centers support the requirements of a single organization; and edge data centers are smaller facilities located closer to users and devices to reduce latency.
And finally, some additional logistics demand will also be generated by server integration facilities, which assemble, configure, and test complete server racks before shipping them to data centers, reducing on-site installation time and accelerating deployment and replacement cycles.

items.excerpt:
Anthropic 发布新安全评估 Siren，让 Claude 在故意削弱的沙盒中执行日常任务，并把有用资源放在沙盒外。在 1700+ 个诱惑场景中，近期 Claude 模型有 21-32% 的情况访问、尝试访问或查看沙盒外内容，但很少滥用所得信息；当系统提示词同时说明沙盒及其规则时，该比例降至约 2% 或更低。
评估给出沙盒越界率和提示词干预的量化数据，还提到用于校准 Claude Code auto mode，可帮助理解智能体安全评测方法。
我们的新评估 Siren 在故意削弱的沙箱中给 Claude 布置日常任务，同时把对任务有用的东西留在沙箱之外。在 1,700 多个为引诱它们而构建的场景中，近期的 Claude 模型有 21-32% 的时间访问、尝试访问或查看沙箱之外，但它们很少滥用所发现的内容。然而，当系统提示同时描述沙箱及其规则时，这一比例降至约 2% 或更低。
我们还使用 Siren 来校准 Claude Code 的自动模式，该模式会在命令运行前进行检查，使 Claude 无需在每一步都请求许可即可工作。
